We will continue to work on enhancements to the program and notify all members as these enhancements are incorporated into the program. The incorporation of a breeding management software The development of a yearly bloodline trade The best format for Species Profiles Tier Three eeees Tf you have any ideas that you would like to see incorporated into the pro- gram, please do not hesitate to contact the FSS Director via email at: kerrimccoy@charter.net , phone: 678-546-3353, fax: 678-546-3352. What YOU can do to make the program more successful: All Finch and Softbill Save members are entitled to free classified advertising in the NFSS Bulletin, on our society website (http://www.NFSS.org) and in the FSS newsletter. We highly recommend that FSS members advertise their available stock so that fellow FSS members can have access to any available bloodlines. Presently, the program does not require FSS partici- pants to sell their offspring to FSS members. We would like however to see FSS members work together by using our free advertising and offering their stock to fellow FSS members whenever feasible. Those who would like to advertise but remain anonymous may contact the FSS Director for more information. We encourage ail FSS participants to recruit fellow hobbyists to join the program. If anyone needs extra program materials to give to an interested party, please do not hesitate to contact the FSS Director. Contribute. Contribute. Contribute. Tier Three and Beyond: The Finch and Softbill Save Committee is currently working on incorporating a Tier Three for the Finch and Softbill Save Program. Tier Three will be geared towards those hobbyists who will adhere to strict record keeping, the required use of specific breeding management software and the re- quired trading of bloodlines on a yearly basis. This level of the program is intended for individuals who may be looking to apply for a cooperative breeding program permit from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, or the Canadian Wildlife Service and for those individuals who are very serious about establishing a genetically viable captive bred population of bird spe- cies. More information on Tier Three will be provided at a later date. Breeder Recognition and Breeder of the Year Awards: The 2002 Finch and Softbill Save program will incorporate recognition awards for its participants. Group Managers and the Finch and Softbill Save Committee will assist the FSS Director in choosing worthy participants to award Breeder Recognition awards on a yearly basis. The NFSS Board of Directors will choose a participant to award the Breeder of the Year award with input provided by the F5S committee. To be eligible for such an award you must be able to demonstrate breeding success with your registered specie(s) and have completed ail FSS required quarterly reports. More de- tails on eligibility will be forthcoming. Many have worked hard at establish- ing species in aviculture and, will be honored for doing so. Membership Fee: In order to incorporate a newsletter, and breeder recognition and breeder of the year awards we must have funds. Presently, the NFSS is not in a position financially to fund these program changes. Awhile back a survey was generated to test the waters and the vast majority of individuals had no problem with paying a membership fee to participate in the Finch and Softbill Save program provided the ideas presented were incorporated into the program and that the membership fee paid was used solely for the pro- gram. We have chosen through the help of tbe survey, to set the cost for participation in the program at $15 yearly. All Finch and Softbill Save par- ticipants must pay a $15 yearly membership fee and remain NFSS mem- bers in good standing. Failure to renew your NFSS membership will result in your expulsion from the Finch and Softbill Save Program, The member- ship fee will be mailed in with your FSS application to the FSS Director, made payable to NFSS.
